summary: Review identified 17 issue(s) (1 critical, 4 high, 12 medium). Code lacks automated test coverage for the modified logic.

findings.title: Dangerous eval() on variable input
findings.root_cause: eval() called with dynamic or variable input, enabling arbitrary code execution
findings.description: eval() called with dynamic or variable input, enabling arbitrary code execution.
findings.impact: An attacker who controls or influences the input can execute arbitrary Python commands with the application's privileges.
findings.recommendation: Avoid eval(). For evaluating data structures safely, use ast.literal_eval().
findings.reproduction_scenario: An attacker who controls or influences the input can execute arbitrary Python commands with the application's privileges.

findings.title: Hardcoded credential detected
findings.root_cause: A secret credential, API key, or authentication token is hardcoded in source
findings.description: A secret credential, API key, or authentication token is hardcoded in source.
findings.impact: Hardcoded credentials in version control can be leaked or stolen, compromising backend services and sensitive user data.
findings.recommendation: Load sensitive secrets from environment variables or a secure secret manager (e.g. os.getenv('API_KEY')).
findings.reproduction_scenario: Hardcoded credentials in version control can be leaked or stolen, compromising backend services and sensitive user data.

findings.title: Potential ZeroDivisionError on empty collection
findings.root_cause: Division by len() without verifying that the collection is non-empty crashes on empty input
findings.description: Division by len() without verifying that the collection is non-empty crashes on empty input.
findings.impact: Calling this function with an empty list or collection triggers ZeroDivisionError and crashes the process.
findings.recommendation: Add an upfront guard: if not numbers: return 0.0 before performing division.
findings.reproduction_scenario: Calling this function with an empty list or collection triggers ZeroDivisionError and crashes the process.

findings.title: Unsafe pickle deserialization
findings.description: pickle.loads() executes arbitrary bytecode during deserialization of untrusted payloads.
findings.impact: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle allows remote code execution (RCE).
findings.recommendation: Do not use pickle for untrusted input. Use safe data formats like json or protocol buffers.
findings.reproduction_scenario: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle allows remote code execution (RCE).

findings.title: Potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
findings.root_cause: HTTP request dispatched to user-supplied dynamic URL without validation or IP allowlisting
findings.description: HTTP request dispatched to user-supplied dynamic URL without validation or IP allowlisting.
findings.impact: Attackers can provide internal network URLs (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost) to access cloud metadata or intranet services.
findings.recommendation: Validate destination URLs against an allowlist of approved domains and block loopback/private IP ranges. (Note: No suggested fix was provided.)
findings.reproduction_scenario: Attackers can provide internal network URLs (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost) to access cloud metadata or intranet services.

findings.title: Weak cryptographic hash algorithm (hashlib.md5)
findings.description: hashlib.md5() is vulnerable to collision attacks and is cryptographically broken.
findings.impact: Attackers can generate hash collisions to forge signatures, bypass checksum validation, or crack passwords.
findings.recommendation: Use modern secure hash algorithms such as hashlib.sha256() or hashlib.sha3_256().
findings.reproduction_scenario: Attackers can generate hash collisions to forge signatures, bypass checksum validation, or crack passwords.

findings.title: SQL Injection in `get_user`
findings.root_cause: User input is directly included in the SQL query without sanitization.
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT id, name, balance FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"
findings.description: This query is vulnerable to SQL injection because user_id is directly inserted into the SQL string without proper escaping.
findings.impact: An attacker could inject malicious SQL code if they provide a specially crafted user_id.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection. (Note: Suggested fix contains invalid Python syntax.)
findings.reproduction_scenario: An attacker could inject malicious SQL code if they provide a specially crafted user_id.
